_comment: Host-specific BLFS review decisions for `server`. Merged on top of recipes/blfs-overrides.json by bin/extract-blfs.py, page by page and block by block, so a page keeps its shared decisions and takes only the hardware-bound ones from here. Every entry must name a concrete GPU, CPU, device or path -- if a decision is true of any LFS box, it belongs in the shared file.

2.cmd:
_restore_resolv() {
    rm -f /etc/resolv.conf
    ln -sf /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf
}
trap _restore_resolv EXIT
rm -f /etc/resolv.conf
printf 'nameserver 1.1.1.1\nnameserver 8.8.8.8\n' > /etc/resolv.conf

mkdir build &&
cd    build &&

meson setup ..                    \
      --prefix=$XORG_PREFIX       \
      --buildtype=release         \
      -D platforms=x11,wayland    \
      -D gallium-drivers=nouveau  \
      -D vulkan-drivers=nouveau   \
      -D valgrind=disabled        \
      -D video-codecs=all         \
      -D libunwind=disabled       \
      -D glvnd=enabled           &&

ninja
2.reason:
Driver scope and the glvnd/Vulkan options are bound to this machine's GPU, so they live here rather than in the shared file. This block is the only reason blfs-mesa is a host recipe at all.

gallium-drivers=nouveau (book default: auto). Decided with the operator 2026-08-25: this box's only GPU is a GTX 770 (GK104, Kepler). auto builds every vendor's driver -- AMD (r300/r600/radeonsi), Intel (iris/crocus), virgl, svga -- none of which this hardware will ever use. nouveau covers the real GPU; llvmpipe is the book's own recommended software-rendering backup and comes in regardless.

vulkan-drivers=nouveau (was empty, then enabled on the 2026-08-26 rebuild). NVK, Mesa's Vulkan driver for NVIDIA hardware, officially supports Kepler (GeForce 600/700, this card included) per Mesa's own docs -- not experimental for this GPU. Needs Linux 6.6+ (this system runs 6.18.10). Kepler is capped at Vulkan 1.2 by hardware (no vulkanMemoryModel, required for 1.3+) even though NVK claims 1.4 conformance for newer generations: a hardware ceiling, not a driver gap. NVK does not share code with the gallium state tracker -- the OpenGL/VAAPI path that has a confirmed crash bug on this card (see BUILD-REPORT.md's GPU deep-dive) -- so that bug does not carry over. vulkan-loader was already installed; the book's circular-dependency note is about libva and does not apply here.

glvnd=enabled (book default: auto), added on the 2026-08-26 rebuild. This is a meson type:feature option, and Mesa was originally built before libglvnd existed, so auto detected no glvnd and defaulted to disabled -- Mesa installed a standalone libEGL.so.1.0.0 with no glvnd vendor ABI. libglvnd's own libEGL.so.1.1.0 later won the /usr/lib/libEGL.so.1 soname, with no vendor JSON in /usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d telling it where to dispatch, so real EGL calls had nothing behind them. A hand-written vendor JSON cannot fix it: the standalone libEGL.so.1.0.0 implements only the direct EGL ABI, not glvnd's vendor entry points. A Mesa rebuild is the only fix. Anything building Mesa alongside libglvnd needs this option set explicitly rather than left on auto, whatever the GPU -- the ordering trap is not NVIDIA-specific.

GLX needs no equivalent option (checked 2026-08-26, no rebuild): Mesa's src/glx/meson.build has no vendor-JSON step at all, it only builds libGLX_mesa.so.0 under glvnd. libglvnd's GLX vendor selection is file-less -- libGLX.so queries the X server per screen via the GLX_EXT_libglvnd extension. That mattered under XWayland, which does not implement the extension and needed __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=mesa in the session launcher; it is moot now that this box runs a real Xorg server, and is recorded only because it explains why no GLX option appears above.

platforms=x11,wayland is the book default and is left alone deliberately. This box abandoned Wayland (see AWESOME-X11-PLAN.md), so the wayland platform is dead weight here, but dropping it would mean rebuilding Mesa to match a recipe change that buys nothing. Recorded as a known, deliberate no-op rather than silently trimmed.

Fix 2026-09-08: this override cmd was missing the book's own 'mkdir build && cd build &&' prefix (still present in the unmodified shared candidate, recipes/blfs-mesa.sh) -- an editing mistake from whenever this override was first written, only ever exercised now on a genuine fresh build. Without it, meson ran directly from the source directory with a bare '..' argument, which meson resolved as builddir=/sources (cwd's parent) and srcdir=/sources/mesa-26.1.7 (cwd) -- a real failure: 'Build directory /sources cannot be a parent of source directory /sources/mesa-26.1.7'.

DNS fix prepended 2026-09-08 (second fix this session): mesa's NVK/NAK rust compiler component (src/compiler/rust/meson.build) declares a hard dependency on the 'syn' crate via meson's own cargo-wrap subproject mechanism, fetched directly from crates.io -- unlike wayland/wayland-protocols above, there is no equivalent real BLFS/distro package for a single vendored Rust crate; this is the same class of live-fetch-at-build-time already fixed for blfs-rust/blfs-cbindgen/blfs-rust-bindgen (this chroot has no working /etc/resolv.conf by default). Confirmed via a real failure: 'Run-time dependency syn found: NO' then a failed crates.io download.

1.cmd:
mkdir build &&
cd    build &&

meson setup ..             \
      --prefix=/usr        \
      --buildtype=release  \
      -D enable-docs=false \
      -D enable-wayland=false &&
ninja
1.reason: This host is X11 + awesome, no Wayland anywhere (see AWESOME-X11-PLAN.md) -- wayland-client/wayland-protocols are not installed. libxkbcommon 1.13.2's meson.build defaults enable-wayland to auto and, when it can't find them, tries to build the Wayland xkbcli programs anyway and hard-errors rather than silently skipping them. Host-specific, not shared: laptop's Hyprland/Wayland stack genuinely wants this support.

2.reason:
Adds `chmod u+s /usr/bin/Xorg` to the book's install block. Not a BLFS command -- the 13.1 page says nothing about setuid anywhere -- and not optional on this machine.

This host runs no display manager and no logind session management, so `startx` is launched by an unprivileged user from a console login. Without the setuid bit Xorg cannot take the VT and dies with `xf86OpenConsole: Switching VT failed` (the 13.0 recipe recorded the older wording, `Cannot open virtual console 1 (Permission denied)`). Setuid-root is Xorg's own pre-logind mechanism for VT access and was the standard arrangement for display-manager-less X11 for decades.

Why this is a host decision rather than a shared one: it is a deliberate setuid-root grant, and it is needed only because of how THIS machine starts its session. `laptop` does not build xorg-server at all. A host that gains a display manager or logind should drop it.

Recorded 2026-09-22 after it was lost. The 13.0 recipe carried this chmod as a hand-edit with its rationale in a comment inside a GENERATED file; converting xorg-server from hand() to book() for 13.1 re-extracted the recipe and silently dropped both. The running X server survived only because it still held the old unlinked binary's inode -- the regression would have surfaced as an unbootable desktop at the next restart, with no way to start X from an SSH session to fix it. This is the second casualty of that one conversion; `-D sha1=libgcrypt` was the first and is recorded in recipes/blfs-13.1/overrides.json. As a `replace` it pins the whole block and will mask a future book change to it, so it wants re-reading on the next release bump.

2.cmd:
install -v -dm755 /etc/systemd/scripts

cat > /etc/systemd/scripts/iptables << "EOF"
#!/bin/sh

# Begin /etc/systemd/scripts/iptables

# Insert connection-tracking modules
# (not needed if built into the kernel)
modprobe nf_conntrack
modprobe xt_LOG

# Enable broadcast echo Protection
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts

# Disable Source Routed Packets
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/accept_source_route
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/default/accept_source_route

# Enable TCP SYN Cookie Protection
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_syncookies

# Disable ICMP Redirect Acceptance
# CHANGED from the book's Personal Firewall example, which writes `default` and never
# writes `all`. That leaves redirects accepted: the kernel's IN_DEV_RX_REDIRECTS
# (include/linux/inetdevice.h:126, checked in linux-6.18.49) is an OR of conf/all and
# the per-interface value whenever forwarding is off, and conf/all/accept_redirects
# defaults to 1, so `all` alone decides the answer no matter what the interfaces say.
# `default` is only the template copied into interfaces brought up later, so it cannot
# fix an interface that already exists. Both are written here: `all` closes it now,
# `default` keeps the book's line doing its intended job for interfaces created later.
# The book's other example on the same page (Masquerading Router) does write `all`, so
# this is an inconsistency inside the book, not a disagreement with it.
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/accept_redirects
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/default/accept_redirects

# Do not send Redirect Messages
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/send_redirects
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/default/send_redirects

# Drop Spoofed Packets coming in on an interface, where responses
# would result in the reply going out a different interface.
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter

# Log packets with impossible addresses.
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/log_martians
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/default/log_martians

# be verbose on dynamic ip-addresses  (not needed in case of static IP)
echo 2 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_dynaddr

# disable Explicit Congestion Notification
# too many routers are still ignorant
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_ecn

# Set a known state
iptables -P INPUT   DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT  DROP

# These lines are here in case rules are already in place and the
# script is ever rerun on the fly. We want to remove all rules and
# pre-existing user defined chains before we implement new rules.
iptables -F
iptables -X
iptables -Z

iptables -t nat -F

# Allow local-only connections
iptables -A INPUT  -i lo -j ACCEPT

# Free output on any interface to any ip for any service
# (equal to -P ACCEPT)
iptables -A OUTPUT -j ACCEPT

# Permit answers on already established connections
# and permit new connections related to established ones
# (e.g. port mode ftp)
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Not in the book's example: this box is administered entirely over SSH, and
# the book's own Personal Firewall script does not allow any inbound service,
# SSH included -- applying it unmodified would have locked out the only way
# in. Explicit allow for new inbound SSH connections; the ESTABLISHED,RELATED
# rule above already covers the rest of each session once it exists.
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT

# Not in the book's example: nginx on the WireGuard tunnel only (2026-09-24). New
# inbound HTTP is accepted on wg0 and nowhere else -- not enp6s0, and not tailscale0,
# which tailscaled's own ts-input chain opens wholesale ahead of these rules. That
# is also why nginx binds 10.0.0.4 and loopback by address rather than `listen 80`;
# see hosts/server/overlay/etc/nginx/nginx.conf. No v6 rule: wg0 carries no v6.
iptables -A INPUT -i wg0 -p tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
# VNC (x0vncserver sharing :0, packages.py seq 267) likewise wg0 only; it also
# binds 10.0.0.4 alone, see hosts/server/overlay/etc/systemd/system/x0vncserver.service.
iptables -A INPUT -i wg0 -p tcp --dport 5900 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT

# Everything else is dropped by policy (no LOG rule -- the book's example logs
# every dropped packet, which on an internet-facing host is a constant stream
# of scan/noise traffic; not wanted here, dropped without a paper trail).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IPv6: blocked entirely, same posture as the laptop (hosts/laptop/blfs-overrides.json).
#
# The book's script never touches ip6tables, so v6 would sit at policy ACCEPT with zero
# rules behind a filtered v4 stack, and sshd listens on *:22, v6 included. Until
# 2026-09-22 this block was applied only by ~/Scripts/firewall.sh from the tty1 login
# hook, so a boot without a console login left v6 open; it is here so iptables.service
# owns it. No global v6 address on this box and nothing here needs v6, so the block is
# total -- no ICMPv6, NDP or RA.
ip6tables -P INPUT   DROP
ip6tables -P FORWARD DROP
ip6tables -P OUTPUT  DROP

ip6tables -F
ip6tables -X
ip6tables -Z

# ::1 excepted: `localhost` resolves to ::1 first, and a DROPped loopback connection
# hangs until timeout instead of failing over to 127.0.0.1.
ip6tables -A INPUT  -i lo -j ACCEPT
ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT

# End /etc/systemd/scripts/iptables
EOF
chmod 700 /etc/systemd/scripts/iptables
2.reason: Shared Personal Firewall block verbatim, plus a full IPv6 block (policy DROP on all three ip6tables chains, flushed, ::1 allowed both ways) -- the same posture as the laptop's host block. Operator request 2026-09-22: the server's rules should be loaded by iptables.service, not by ~/Scripts/firewall.sh from the tty1 login hook, which until then was the only thing applying the v6 block here. Host rather than shared for the reason the laptop gives: a posture choice, not a fact about the book. A host block replaces the shared block whole, so any later change to the shared blfs-iptables block has to be pulled through here as well. 2026-09-24: tcp/80 NEW accepted on wg0 only, for nginx (packages.py seq 264), operator-specified exposure 'wireguard and loopback only'. 2026-09-25: tcp/5900 NEW accepted on wg0 only, for x0vncserver (packages.py seq 267), operator-specified 'tigervnc over wireguard'.

5.cmd:
sed -i '/^PermitRootLogin /d;/^PasswordAuthentication /d;/^KbdInteractiveAuthentication /d' \
    /etc/ssh/sshd_config

cat >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config << "EOF"
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
EOF
5.reason: Requested 2026-09-22: no root login, no password login. The book's block 5 (postlfs/openssh.html, 'If you would like to now disable password logins') enabled here; the shared file drops it because a machine without an authorized_keys would be locked out of ssh, which is a fact about the machine, not the book. This machine has john's authorized_keys (~john/.ssh/authorized_keys, carried from the pre-LFS install) and sudo via wheel, so key-only is safe. On a fresh build nothing in packages.py installs that key: ssh is unreachable until it is copied in from the console. Replaced rather than applied verbatim for the reason recorded on laptop's identical decision: sshd honours the FIRST occurrence of a repeated directive, so the book's `>>` appends are not settings when an earlier line exists (the overlay sshd_config deployed here already carries PasswordAuthentication no at line 67). The sed deletes every live line for all three directives, including the one block 3 just appended, and writes exactly one of each. PermitRootLogin is restated so the result does not depend on block 3. Check: `sshd -T | grep -Ei '^(permitrootlogin|passwordauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication) '` should print no for all three.

1.reason: The book's two nettle-4 digest seds are kept as the first lines. No Linux-PAM on this host: it was left out deliberately (server BUILD-REPORT 2026-08-26, 'this system has no PAM installed at all'), and installing the library alone would let later sudo/shadow/openssh/systemd rebuilds detect it and switch to PAM auth with no /etc/pam.d config. Operator chose (2026-09-25) to patch TigerVNC instead. The book lists PAM as Required because TigerVNC's CMakeLists.txt has an unconditional `find_package(PAM REQUIRED)` under UNIX; in the source, PAM is used only by unix/vncserver/vncsession.c (the systemd launcher for the Xvnc sessions the book's configuration section sets up, not used here) and common/rfb/UnixPasswordValidator.cxx (username/password security types). This block removes the check and the vncserver subdirectory, and replaces the validator with one that always refuses. VNC-password auth (VncAuth, TLSVnc, RA2ne) needs no PAM and is what this host uses.
